source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or small only after choosing the thing being counted and a familiar comparison.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Context is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or small only after' is answered as context rather than one lakh.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Context is what produces one lakh, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is one lakh because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or small only after' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: one lakh is settled by running 'Decide the fewest button clicks needed to make a number using': The fewest clicks use the standard place-value decomposition of the number; the minimum — on the item about Decide whether a number such as one lakh is big or.

intelligence.enrichment: The same number can feel large in one context and ordinary in another; one lakh rice varieties or one lakh days is far beyond a usual lifetime, while one lakh people can be discussed through a stadium or population context.
